KeeperFX cannot ship a few files that must come from an original Dungeon Keeper. Pick your Dungeon Keeper folder — the one containing DATA and SOUND — and they are picked out and copied automatically.\n\nA mounted or extracted CD image works too. Nothing else from that folder is copied.

Removes the installation including save games. The folders you imported from are not touched.
Automatic — follow the device last used
Touch — always use the touch scheme
Mouse & keyboard — ignore the touch screen

Tap = left click · hold = right click · drag = paint area · two fingers = pan, pinch to zoom, twist to rotate · two finger tap = right click · three finger tap = back (the map has its own panel button)
The system back button and the back gesture also leave a menu. On screen: a back arrow, and a right click toggle - while it is on, a tap slaps and a drag undesignates.
Show the on screen buttons while playing
Also install the alpha patch for this engine

The engine in this app is built from the current source, and the stable release does not carry everything it expects - the fonts for Japanese, Chinese and Korean among them. The alpha patch adds those, a small download on top of the release. Turn this off to stay strictly on 1.4.0; the patch comes back off without downloading anything.
Sets the language the game runs in. Starts on the one the device uses; speech and text only appear in it when the installation carries that language.
This installation has no texts in %1$s, so the game runs in English.
Every knob here reaches the engine as its -touchtune startup option, so the extra command line options field still overrides them. Changes apply the next time the game starts.
60 divides the display evenly and leaves the phone cool. Unlimited draws as fast as the processor can, which heats it up until everything stutters.
How long a still finger rests before it turns into a right click.
Movement below this still counts as a tap rather than a drag.
Pan threshold (% of the screen height)
How far two fingers travel before the map starts to follow them. It then catches up, so nothing is lost.
Zoom threshold (% of the screen height)
How much the distance between the fingers changes before the map starts to zoom. Raise this if panning keeps turning into zooming.
How far the fingers twist before the map starts to turn. Raise this if panning keeps turning into rotating.
How much speed a released swipe keeps per sixtieth of a second. 0 stops the map dead the moment the fingers lift.
Possession look speed (degrees per pixel at 720 high)
How far the view of a possessed creature turns for the travel of a finger.
Possession stick size (% of the screen height)
Radius of the ring that appears under the thumb. A larger one takes a longer push to start walking.
